verdict.tagline: Hilarious co-op platforming with tight controls and endless user levels.
for_you_if: you want chaotic co-op campaigns with friends
you love tackling challenging platforming levels
you enjoy building custom stages in level editors
not_for_you_if: you rely on standard controller support working instantly
you need stable offline save progression
you play on native Linux systems

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a built-in level creator along with various modes and options.

citations.review_text: I remember laughing until tears playing this game when I was a kid. This game is a gift, bestowed to us by god. You crash on an island full of crazy evil murderous cats that use a magic top hat to corrupt your friend and turn him evil and you have to battle your way deeper into the theatre to rescue him all while collecting gems... and yarn? to sell to an illegal weapons dealer in the theatre while listening to the delightfully hilarious narrator bully you every time you die. I mean... sounds like a good time to me. Oh, there's a ton of prisoners to free (you spend gems to "free prisoners" and get their skins to play as) as well and a whole level editor built in so you can make your own shenanigans too.

Don't turn your back on me!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the controls as tight and responsive, and the mechanics as simple to pick up.

citations.review_text:
My favourite game from Behemoth. 

I played this at release on Xbox way back in the day and it became one of my favourite platformers. 

Didn’t know it had a steam release and had completely forgotten about its existence until I randomly stumbled across it a few days ago on sale. 

The game is just as good as I remember. Tight controls, responsive, great art direction and a wicked sense of humour. 

I can’t recommend this game enough. 

It’s also fantastic in co-op.

Still just as silly and fun as I remember it. I used to play the game with my cousins as a kid and had a blast, especially killing each other in the shop repeatedly with all the weapons. The mechanics are simple to pick up on and trying to complete each level perfectly is actually lots of fun. Many of Behemoth's games are favorites of mine, but this one has a special spot in my heart. I still think of the secret level song all the time (speaking of which, the soundtrack is great). Will Stamper's narration and quips are still so amusing to me, they're the icing holding the whole cake together. 10/10 not just nostalgia, great game overall!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game locks to VSync, resulting in a high refresh rate and smooth experience.

citations.review_text:
Another fun Behemoth game and it's perfect for co-op especially when you use a fireball on each other for like an hour.

Platforming is fun and controls great, levels are fun and the game looks pretty. The narrator is also funny and I would happily sit through a whole hour of him talking non stop.


The Behemoth also recently released a new Quality of Life update that made the game a lot more modern including some fairly good Steam Input implementation to make sure the game continues to be a great experience even on modern hardware and controllers. This is great to see especially for the longevity of the game and its functionality.

The game also locks to VSync so you get a nice high refresh rate and smooth experience.

Good stuff.

BattleBlock Theater is a great puzzle platformer which I thoroughly enjoyed for the humour and level design, though I did wish we had some quicker ways to jump back into the game (instead of having to navigate right form the start before Chapter 1).
Ultimately I completed the story within 9h, allowing for some repeats to best my previous scores - there's still a LOT for me to go through, including the "encore" levels for most before I can hope to get A++ scores for each level.
I feel the game is best enjoyed in short goes - I found it just a bit too repetitive when I tried to binge a chapters at a time, even though it generally does a good job of mixing up the threats and introducing new ones.

I have not yet played the game in co-op mode, so I cannot vouch for that.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the voice acting, comedy, and the narrator as standout parts of the experience.

citations.review_text: Fun game, the last two chapters are a little too difficult for my taste. Would definitely recommend it, great voice acting too.
Good story and the platforming somehow never gets boring! The narrator is the best part though. All in all 10/10

I played the game on Xbox awhile back, I actually completed the game there. I got the game again for Steam because I wanted a not outdated version of BattleBlock Theater y'know like the remaster, online, furbottom's features, etc. 

So far I really like playing this version. But I think that's more so because I just like the game in general. I can't wait to put my levels onto the workshop for yall once I make some.

claims.claim: The story campaign features separate level sets across different modes like Normal and Insane.

citations.review_text:
[b]The Good[/b]
- Extremely solid platforming, the sheer variety of creative ways they created levels in this that utilize a relatively small amount of movement/action options you have at your disposal is extremely impressive. They pack a lot in here. - The game is legitimately funny, the cutscenes' humor got me to laugh out loud at various points and I went back and watched them all multiple times. - The Behemoth's classic, unique, art style is great as always. - This game makes a great co-op experience. It's fun to go through the whole campaign with a friend in levels crafted specifically for two players.

[b]The Bad[/b]
- The game packs in a ton of content, to the point that I would argue it's too much. I think the Story mode would have been more fun if two of the worlds were chopped off and only the best levels kept. You have the Community Theatre mode for players that just want more and more infinite challenges of platforming stages. The Story mode should be a best-hits selection of what the game has to offer, but by the end of eight Chapters it definitely is feeling long in the tooth. That's 112 levels just to get through the Story mode once! (And the set of Story mode levels are unique for Normal Solo, Insane Mode Solo, Normal Coop, and Insane Mode Coop. So even if there had only been six Chapters in the Story mode there would have been plenty of content here to keep platforming fanatics satisfied.) - There is an achievement attached to collecting all of the prisoner heads called "Freedom Hero". Prisoners are bought in the shop by spending gems you pick up throughout the game. There are a whopping 256 possible prisoners in the game which is great considering they are purely cosmetic... but attaching an achievement for collecting all of them turns this into a HUGE chore for any completionist. To collect enough gems to buy them all, you can play through the Story mode FOUR TIMES (in Solo and Coop, both on Normal and Insane difficulty, because you can't re-colle…

Definitely a fun game. Great fun on your own, but even more so with a friend. Weapons are a bit overpowered in certain circumstances (Dart Gun can be used to cheese some puzzles by climbing walls and reaching areas you're not supposed to, and other weapons could be used in similar or different/better ways), but I think the Devs planned for that, as you're not punished for doing that.

As for a quick description of the game, it's a puzzle platformer. You're incentivized to go fast to get the A++ rank, which isn't too hard to get, but will require you to replay the levels several times to get them. The levels, even on Insane difficulty (a mode that restarts the level you're on when you die even once), are fairly challenging. I highly recommend playing this game with a friend, as it's very fun to do so!

The only downside to this game that I can think of is that the Singleplayer levels and Multiplayer levels are very similar, with only slight changes between to take advantage of the Multiplayer moves, or modified to be completable by a single player, making a second playthrough on your own rather repetitive, especially if you want to get 100% completion, which would require you to play through the same set of levels 4 times over, and this game isn't short at all, at least if you're going for all A++'s, which aren't required. Another downside, at least to me, is this game's obsession with potty humor, specifically with feces. I don't get why, but pretty much every cutscene in the game has some reference to poop either visually, spoken, or both, and it get's rather gross after a while, especially on the fourth playthrough to get all the playthroughs. That being said, the writing for the game is absolutely hilarious, and if you don't end up getting this game, at least do yourself the favor of watching the opening cinematic.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the developers removed native Linux support following a recent update or remaster, breaking installs for Linux users.

citations.review_text: Removed native linux support 12 years after release. Odd move. https://steamdb.info/app/238460/history/?changeid=35896013

This game originally started with good native Linux support and then they executed a rug-pull, switching everyone's install to the Windows version without warning or recourse. I would not recommend supporting this company at all, or any companies that behave similarly. If the Windows version was actually even working I would still be upset, but additionally this broke my install, when just days prior the Linux version was still running excellently for me.
